The matching paper is Retrieval Improvements Do Not Guarantee Better Answers: A Study of RAG for AI Policy QA by Saahil Mathur, Ryan David Rittner, Vedant Ajit Thakur, et al. [1] It studies RAG for AI governance and policy analysis on the AGORA corpus of 947 AI policy documents, using a ColBERT-based retriever fine-tuned with contrastive learning and a generator aligned with Direct Preference Optimization. [1]

Its main result is that better retrieval metrics did not consistently improve end-to-end policy question answering. [1] The paper reports that stronger retrieval could even produce more confident hallucinations when relevant documents were missing from the corpus, and frames this as a reliability concern for policy-focused RAG systems over dynamic regulatory corpora. [1]
